filename: Navigating the Noise_ Bringing Clarity to ML Parameterization Design with O(100) Ensembles.pdf
title: Navigating the Noise: Bringing Clarity to ML Parameterization Design with O(100) Ensembles
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems (JAMES)
parameterization_target: atmospheric subgrid heating and moistening tendencies (dT/dt and dq/dt)
code_availability: Version v2 of spcam3.0-neural-net-spreadtesting is preserved at https://zenodo.org/records/11392025 and developed at https://github.com/SciPritchardLab/spcam3.0-neural-net. v4 of ClimScale is preserved at https://zenodo.org/records/14252488 and developed at https://github.com/SciPritchardLab/ClimScale.
testbed_rationale: Provides ClimScale, an open, standardized, end-to-end pipeline linking offline training (KerasTuner) with online coupled evaluation (Fortran-Keras Bridge in SPCAM3) at scale, designed specifically for ML parameterization benchmarking.
pain_points: Divergence between offline and online performance metrics: lower offline error does not imply better online error or online stability (e.g., MAE loss improves offline error and stability but worsens online error; removing dropout reduces online error but increases crashes).
Frequent online numerical instability and simulation crashes when coupled to the host GCM.
Emergent noise and high variance across hyperparameter selections mask causal differences between ML design configurations unless evaluated with O(100) ensemble sizes.
Persistent structural zonal mean temperature biases (stratospheric cold bias and high-latitude warm bias) across coupled simulations.
Technical bottleneck of automating coupling across hundreds to thousands of distinct neural network parameterizations inside a climate model.
extraction_notes: Manuscript submitted to JAMES; revision 3 on arXiv (December 2024). Online error size was calculated using 8 longitudinally subsampled points to save disk storage.
